blocks.text: Your laptop arrives with everything installed. The first sign-in takes about twenty minutes.
Steps
Sign in with the temporary password from your welcome email and choose a new one.
Set up multi-factor sign-in on your phone.
Open email, calendar, Teams and the HR portal once each so they finish setting up.
Stuck?
Ask the Ask AI box on the onboarding site, or raise a ticket with IT help. Day-one tickets are answered first.

blocks.text: Every new joiner has a buddy: a colleague from a neighboring team who has been here at least a year. Your buddy is not your manager. They are the person to ask the questions you think are too small to ask.
Your first conversation
Book thirty minutes in your first two days, over coffee if you are in the office.
Ask how they plan their week and which meetings matter.
Agree when you will meet again. Most pairs meet weekly for the first month.

blocks.text: A few minutes now saves confusion in an emergency. Read this before your first full week in the office.
In an emergency
Fire exits are marked in green on every floor. Assembly point: the square in front of the main entrance.
First aiders are listed at reception and on every kitchen noticeboard.
Call reception on extension 100 for anything urgent.
Your workstation
Adjust your chair and screen height before you start. Ask facilities for a footrest, a second screen or a standing desk if you need one.

blocks.text: If you spend money on behalf of Keystone Dynamics, you get it back quickly. Here is what you can claim and how.
What you can claim
Travel booked through the company travel tool.
Meals while travelling, up to the daily allowance for that country.
Equipment approved in advance by your manager.
How to claim
Photograph the receipt and submit it in the expenses app within 30 days. Claims approved by the 20th are paid with that month's salary.

blocks.text: We work hybrid. Teams agree their own rhythm, with at least two shared office days a week so people can meet in person.
How it works
Core hours are 10:00 to 16:00 in your local time, so meetings fit everyone.
Agree your office days with your manager and book a desk in advance.
Flexible start and finish times are fine as long as your team knows how to reach you.
Time off
Request leave in the HR portal at least two weeks ahead for anything longer than three days. Your manager approves it there.

blocks.text: Keeping customer and company data safe is part of every role here, not only IT's. This page covers the rules that matter most in your first weeks.
The essentials
Lock your screen whenever you step away from your desk.
Use the company password manager and turn on multi-factor sign-in for every tool.
Share files through approved tools only, never through personal email or storage.
Report a lost device or a suspicious message to IT the same day.
Why it matters
Most incidents start with one ordinary click. A fast report turns a serious incident into a small one, so you will never be blamed for reporting quickly.

blocks.text: Our Code of Conduct is how we work with each other, with customers and with partners. It is short on purpose. Read it once now, and come back to it whenever a decision feels unclear.
What we expect from everyone
Treat colleagues, customers and partners with respect, in every channel and every language.
Be honest about what you know, what you do not know and what went wrong.
Protect customer data as if it were your own.
Speak up when something does not feel right. Raising a concern in good faith is always safe.
Where to raise a concern

Talk to your manager first when you can. If that does not feel right, contact your People partner or use the confidential Speak Up line listed on the People Hub. Every report is reviewed by someone outside your reporting line.
Acknowledge this page
Use the acknowledge button at the end of this page to confirm you have read the Code. It ticks this step off in your onboarding journey.

acknowledgment.message: I have read and understood the Code of Conduct.
